To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the maximum conductivity of solid systems of the form AgX 1 –CdX 2 occurs for a concentration that depends on the compressibility of the solid solution and on the difference between the compressibilities of the two end-members.
the maximum electrical conductivity in mixed crystals of the AgX–CdI 2 system occurs for 20 mol % CdI 2.

a maximum in the electrical conductivity of mixed crystals is predicted to occur when (1) the concentration of the minority component is close to 20 mol%, (2) the compressibility of the mixed crystal is close to that of the pure major component, and (3) the compressibility ratio of the mixed crystal to the pure major component is close to the square of the compressibility ratio.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrical conductivity in the AgX–CdCl 2 and AgBr–CdBr 2 systems.
the development of a quantitative understanding of the electrical conductivity in mixed crystals of the type AgX–CdI 2.
the electrical conductivity of multiphased solid solutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the maximum in the electrical conductivity in the AgX–CdCl 2 (or AgX–CdBr 2 ) systems is caused by the fact that, in the vicinity of the maximum, the compressibility of the solid solutions is very high.

the maximum in conductivity is due to an optimum in the compressibility of the mixed crystals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the conductivity of solid systems is a complex function of the composition, temperature, and the pressure of the system, and it may have a maximum at a certain composition, temperature, or pressure, or at a certain combination of these parameters.
the maximum conductivity in the mixed crystals is due to the maximum compressibility of the crystal lattice, i.e., the maximum number of vacancies in the lattice.

a conductivity maximum is observed when a mixed crystal has a compressibility that is larger than that of the pure component, and that a conductivity maximum can occur only if the mixed crystal does not have a phase separation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the electrical conductivity of mixed crystals is determined by both the concentration dependence of the compressibility and the concentration dependence of other parameters, such as the mobility of charge carriers.
the electrical conductivity of mixed crystals can be used as an indicator of the compressibility of the crystal.

the conductivity maximum in the silver halide-cadmium halide solid systems is not an anomalous phenomenon, but rather it is a consequence of a simple model that is based on a single parameter, namely the compressibility of the solid solution.
